title: Types of Visa in Dubai
description: Discover the ultimate guide to understanding the various types of visas in Dubai, UAE. Plan your stay and navigate the visa process effectively

contentHtml:
Dubai has solidly established itself as one of the top commercial and tourist destinations in the globe. And the welcoming visa policy is much to credit for its appeal. There are many different types of visa in Dubai that cater to a broad variety of needs; ranging from disaster migration to medical treatment and more. Therefore, knowing the types of visa in UAE can be helpful for anyone wanting to come to the region.

In this article, we will talk about the types of visa in Dubai. Coming to Dubai can be a great experience for anyone. However, it is vital that people come holding the right types of visa in UAE. As a result, to help you send a successful application, you can count on Connect Group and the following information. Let us see:

1. Types of visa in Dubai

2. Frequently asked questions about visa types in Dubai

3. How can Connect Group help you?

1. Types of visa in Dubai

Since they are well-known international commerce hubs and well-liked vacation spots, Dubai and other UAE regions get a sizable volume of visa requests from tourists, prospective employees, and business travelers. Thus, depending on why you are visiting, the government issues a variety of entry permits and visas. The four most prevalent forms of types of Dubai visa are business, transit, and tourist visas.

1.1 E-visa for GCC residents

GCC citizens who wish to visit Dubai may do so by requesting an e-visa. It is valid up until 30 days after obtaining it, but if it expires, you can extend it for an additional 30 days.

To acquire these types of visa in Dubai, you must:

  • Be an authorized GCC resident (valid for more than three months after the date of arrival).
  • Have a current passport (valid for at least 3 months after your arrival date).

Conditions

  • In short, after their application is approved, GCC citizens will receive their e-visa at the email address they have on file.
  • Residents of the GCC will not be permitted to enter Dubai if their occupation has changed since they were issued an entry permit.
  • Also, if the sponsoring person is not taking GCC nationals with them on their trip, the visa application cannot be approved.

1.2 Golden Visa

People from all over the world can live, work, and study in the UAE thanks to one of the long-term residency permits known as the Golden Visa. These visa types in Dubai are issued for periods of ten or five years and people can renew them automatically.

UAE Golden Visa holders can be:

  • Real estate investors.
  • Ph.D. holders in the region.
  • Investors.
  • Entrepreneurs.
  • Engineers from the UAE who specialize in electronics, programming, biotechnology, and computer science.
  • Experts in biotechnology engineering, genetic engineering, big data, software engineering, computer engineering, artificial intelligence, electronics engineering, and epidemiology and viruses.
  • Top high school graduates from the UAE and their families.

Being a legal resident of the UAE entitles you to:

  • Create a bank account and gain access to financial resources
  • Apply for a driver’s license and gain access to government health care and health insurance.
  • Register his/her children in public and private schools, work and invest, and travel visa-free to specific destinations.

The sort of service and visa type you apply for will have a significant impact on the cost of your Dubai Golden Visa. The cost of a Dubai Golden Visa ranges from AED 2,800 to AED 3,800 if you request it from the United Arab Emirates. The price of the Golden Visa is from AED 3,800 to AED 4,800 if you apply from outside the nation.

1.3 Real Estate Investor Visa

These types of UAE visa are one of the unique Dubai visas intended to promote real estate investment in the nation. There are two sorts:

You would have to satisfy the following criteria to be granted an investment visa for ten years:

  • Create a new business with an investment capital of at least AED 10 million.
  • Forming a partnership in an established business with a minimum investment of AED 10 million
  • Possess deposits totaling a minimum of AED 10 million in any UAE emirate.
  • Make sure that out of the AED 10 million invested, 60%, or AED 6 million, are placed in markets beyond the real estate market.

On the other hand, a 5-year investor visa is an option as well. The following are the prerequisites:

  • An investment in real estate of at least AED 5 million
  • The amount is not lendable.
  • Property must be kept for a minimum of three years.

1.4 Dubai Business Visa

The Gold Card Visa system includes the UAE Business Visa as a key component of it. At a certain point in their careers, foreign business owners who have established their enterprises may apply for this permit. The following qualifications are required for a UAE work visa:

  • Verification of your business experience.
  • A senior position in a firm or a shareholder in a start-up.
  • Desire to go to the UAE.
  • Possessing a concrete business concept or plan.

These visa types Dubai permit is also available for dependents of holders of business visas.

1.5 Dubai Medical Visas

Those traveling to the city for medical care are given the Patient Entry Permit, also referred to as the Dubai Medical Visa. Both victims and their guests may enter with these entry permits. There are two primary types of visas in UAE:

  • Only one entry for Patient and companion entry authorizations.
  • Multiple-entry Patient and companion entry authorizations.

Hospitals in Dubai offer cutting-edge care for a range of medical and aesthetic requirements. Your sponsor must submit an application to the General Directorate of Residency and Foreigners Affairs in order to get a Dubai Medical Visa (GDRFA). Your sponsor must provide these things in order for your visa to be approved:

  • A photocopied passport.
  • A letter outlining your illness and the rationale behind your visit from your hospital.
  • Evidence of financial stability.
  • Proof of health insurance.

1.6 Retirement Visas for UAE Residents

Another unique visa category in Dubai is the retirement visa. In the region, retirees who are 55 years of age or older may apply for a long-term residency visa. If one of the following requirements is satisfied, the retirement visa in Dubai may be extended for an additional five years:

  • If the retiree purchases a home for AED 2 million.
  • When any senior has up to AED 1 million in savings.
  • if the retiree makes AED 20k a month in active income.

1.7 Remote Working UAE Visa

Many industries have adjusted their working patterns as a result of the pandemic, and many workers now opt to work remotely. This means that whether you work for a firm or as a freelancer, you can operate from anywhere in the globe. The UAE government issued a one-year residence visa for such individuals. The following are the visa requirements:

  • A passport that is valid for at least six months.
  • Health coverage.
  • Evidence of employment/ownership.
  • A one-year employment contract is required.
  • Previous pay stubs three months prior to bank statements.
  • A monthly income of a minimum of USD 5,000 is necessary.

1.8 Event Visas in Dubai

These next types of visas in Dubai are for those who want to attend exhibits, conferences, or other events in Dubai. Likewise, it is identical to a Dubai tourist visa and people cannot apply for a renewal of these types of visa in Dubai. Therefore, to file for an Event Visa, please send the following documents:

  • A copy of a valid passport (or valid for at least three months).
  • A copy of the sponsor’s visa and passport page.

1.9 Permit for one year of residency for those affected by war or catastrophes

Citizens of nations impacted by conflicts and natural catastrophes can also seek residency in Dubai, according to a resolution made by the UAE Cabinet in 2018. The residency period in Dubai is one year. Wives, divorced women, and kids can extend their visas without the need for a sponsor once.

1.10 Sponsor parents as a student in the UAE

The UAE government has announced the availability of a special visa for foreign students studying there. Students will be able to sponsor their families or other relatives with this unique Dubai visa as long as they have the financial wherewithal to do so, covering housing. Families’ sponsored student visas will soon receive more information.

2. Frequently asked questions about visa types in Dubai

Here are some frequently asked questions about the types of visa in Dubai. Let us observe:

2.1 How many different Dubai visa types are available for UAE travelers?

As a famous tourist destination, Dubai offers a variety of visa options to visitors from all around the globe. Thus, there are several UAE visa types available, ranging from tourist to student. Subsequently, expats working in the emirate frequently have work permits in Dubai.

2.2 How can I renew my tourist visa in UAE?

In Dubai, you can renew your tourist visa twice for a period of 30 days.

2.3 In the UAE, how do I cancel a residency visa?

Only sponsors are authorized to revoke a visitor’s residency permit in the United Arab Emirates (UAE); however, this is according visa regulations and other guidelines.

2.4 Can I get a visa in Dubai on arrival?

Some countries’ nationals can obtain a visa upon arrival in Dubai. Do not forget to check out the requirements for these UAE visa types to see if you qualify for a visa on arrival in Dubai.

2.5 How much does a three-month visa to Dubai cost?

A 90-day visitor visa in Dubai costs AED 1,000. If you want to learn more about visit visas in Dubai, see our Dubai visa services.
